hindi: अधम लोग धन चाहते हैं, मध्यम धन और मान चाहते हैं; उत्तम लोग मान चाहते हैं; मान ही महान् लोगों का धन है।
english: The lowest desire wealth, the middling wealth and honour; the best desire honour; honour indeed is the wealth of the great.
notes: Verb icchanti is carried over to 'dhanamānau ca madhyamāḥ'; dhana-mānau is read as a dvandva in the accusative dual, 'wealth and honour'.

hindi: ईख, जल, दूध, मूल, पान, फल, औषध: खाकर भी स्नान, दान आदि क्रियाएँ करनी चाहिए।
english: Sugarcane, water, milk, root, betel, fruit, medicine: even having eaten, acts such as bathing and giving are to be performed.
notes: The first line is a bare list of items; its relation to 'bhakṣayitvā' is understood (items eaten). āpaḥ is plural in Sanskrit.

hindi: दीपक अन्धकार को खाता है और काजल उत्पन्न होता है; जो अन्न नित्य खाया जाता है, वैसी सन्तान उत्पन्न होती है।
english: The lamp eats darkness and soot is produced; whatever food one eats constantly, such offspring is born.
notes: prasūyate can also be taken as active 'produces' (lamp as subject); passive with kajjalam as subject is preferred. In the second line the subject of bhakṣayate is not expressed ('one'); Hindi uses the passive for this. 'yat annam' has no 'tat' in the Sanskrit.

hindi: हे बुद्धिमान्, गुणों से युक्त लोगों को धन दो, और कहीं मत दो। समुद्र से प्राप्त जल मेघ के मुख में सदा माधुर्य से युक्त है। स्थावर और जंगम सभी जीवों को, भूमण्डल को जीवित करके, उसी को फिर करोड़ गुना होकर समुद्र की ओर जाते हुए देखो।
english: O wise one, give wealth to those endowed with qualities; do not give anywhere else. Water received from the ocean in the mouth of the cloud is always endowed with sweetness. Having revived all living beings, the unmoving and the moving, the orb of the earth, see that very water again, multiplied ten-millionfold, going to the ocean.
notes: Four printed lines form one verse (two halves of a longer metre, 19 syllables each); the first two lines are the statement and the last two a comparison. 'gacchantam' is a masculine accusative form, while 'tat' (neuter) would take 'gacchat'; it is read as 'that (water) going to the ocean', and the metre supports the printed form. 'na ... kvacit' is read as 'not anywhere'. 'tat' is taken to refer to the jalam of line b; the text does not say 'water' in line d.

hindi: हजारों चाण्डालों द्वारा और तत्त्व को देखने वाले विद्वानों द्वारा एक यवन ही कहा गया है; यवन से परे कोई नीच नहीं है।
english: By thousands of cāṇḍālas and by learned seers of truth, one yavana indeed is declared; no one lower is beyond a yavana.
notes: The first line is elliptic: 'proktaḥ' has no predicate and the case of 'cāṇḍālānām sahasraiḥ' (genitive plus instrumental) leaves the construction open; the literal rendering is kept, with the instrumentals taken as agents of 'proktaḥ'. An alternative reading takes the line as a comparison ('one yavana is declared equal to thousands of cāṇḍālas'), but the Sanskrit does not say so. 'paraḥ' is read as 'beyond/other'.

words.gloss: in the smoke of the pyre

hindi: तेल की मालिश में, चिता के धुएँ में, मैथुन में, क्षौरकर्म में, वह तब तक चाण्डाल होता है जब तक स्नान न करे।
english: In oil-massage, in the smoke of the pyre, in sexual union, in shaving, he is a cāṇḍāla as long as he does not perform a bath.
notes: The subject 'he' is not expressed. 'ca' after 'na' joins the clause to the list of occasions and is left untranslated as it adds no separate sense. 'citādhūme' read as 'smoke of the funeral pyre'.

words.gloss: at the end of the meal

hindi: अजीर्ण में जल औषध है, पच जाने पर जल बल देने वाला है; और भोजन में जल अमृत है, भोजन के अन्त में विष को हरने वाला।
english: In indigestion water is medicine, once digested water gives strength; and in a meal water is nectar, at the end of the meal it removes poison.
notes: 'jīrṇe' is read as 'when (the food is) digested', locative absolute, with the noun not stated.

hindi: क्रियाहीन ज्ञान हत है और अज्ञान से मनुष्य हत है; नायकहीन सेना हत है; पतिहीन स्त्रियाँ निश्चय ही नष्ट हैं।
english: Knowledge devoid of action is destroyed and a man through ignorance is destroyed; a leaderless army is destroyed; husbandless women are indeed lost.
notes: The printed 'nirṇāyakam' is nir-nāyakam (the n becomes ṇ after r by internal sandhi). In the Hindi, 'हत' renders hata and 'नष्ट' renders naṣṭa.

hindi: बुढ़ापे के समय पत्नी का मर जाना, धन का बन्धु के हाथ में चला जाना और भोजन का दूसरे के अधीन होना: पुरुषों की तीन विडम्बनाएँ हैं।
english: A wife dead in old age, wealth gone into a kinsman's hand and food dependent on another: three mockeries of men.
notes: viḍambanā is rendered 'mockery' (also 'distress, imitation'). The compound 'bandhuhasta' has no number marked; 'a kinsman's hand' is the literal reading.

hindi: अग्निहोत्र के बिना वेद नहीं, और दान के बिना क्रिया नहीं; भाव के बिना सिद्धि नहीं; इसलिए भाव ही कारण है।
english: No Vedas without the agnihotra, and no rite without a gift; no accomplishment without inner feeling; therefore inner feeling is indeed the cause.
notes: bhāva is rendered 'inner feeling' (also 'disposition, faith'); the same rendering is used in the next units.

words.gloss: in what is made of clay

hindi: देवता न काष्ठ में मिलता है, न पत्थर में, न मिट्टी से बने में; भाव में ही देवता मिलता है; इसलिए भाव ही कारण है।
english: A god is not found in wood, nor in stone, nor in what is made of clay; in inner feeling indeed a god is found; therefore inner feeling is indeed the cause.
notes: The printed 'mṛṇmaye' is mṛt-maye (t becomes ṇ before m). 'vidyate' is read as 'is found'; 'exists' is also possible.

hindi: काष्ठ, पाषाण और धातुओं की भाव से सेवा करके और श्रद्धा से, इस प्रकार उसकी सिद्धि विष्णु की कृपा से होती है।
english: Having done service of wood, stone and metals with inner feeling and with faith, thus his accomplishment comes through the grace of Viṣṇu.
notes: The construction 'sevanam' with a genitive of the materials is literal: 'service of wood, stone and metals'. 'tathā' is read as 'thus'. The sentence has no verb; 'comes' is supplied by the copula sense. The unit carries no further explanation of what is served.

hindi: शान्ति के समान तप नहीं है, सन्तोष से बढ़कर सुख नहीं; तृष्णा से बड़ा रोग नहीं, और दया से बढ़कर धर्म नहीं।
english: There is no austerity equal to tranquillity, no happiness greater than contentment; no disease greater than craving, and no dharma beyond compassion.
notes: 'dayāparaḥ' parallels 'santoṣāt param' and 'tṛṣṇāyāḥ paraḥ' and is read as 'beyond compassion'; the compound could also mean 'having compassion as its highest', but the sense of the parallel is kept.

hindi: क्रोध वैवस्वत राजा है, तृष्णा वैतरणी नदी है; विद्या कामदुधा धेनु है, सन्तोष नन्दन वन है।
english: Anger is the king Vaivasvata, craving the river Vaitaraṇī; learning is the wish-milking cow, contentment the Nandana grove.

text_flags.why: Likely typo: 'denuḥ' is not a word; 'dhenuḥ' (cow) fits kāma-dudhā and the Devanāgarī देनुः shows the same omission.
Possible: the usual form of the stem is from √duh with dugh-, 'kāmadughā'; 'dudhā' is not a regular form.

notes: Proper names are kept without added identification, as the line does not state who Vaivasvata is. The words list uses the corrected 'dhenuḥ' for 'denuḥ'; 'kāma-dudhā' is kept as printed.

hindi: गुण रूप को सुशोभित करता है, शील कुल को सुशोभित करता है; सिद्धि विद्या को सुशोभित करती है, भोग धन को सुशोभित करता है।
english: Quality adorns beauty, good conduct adorns the family; accomplishment adorns learning, enjoyment adorns wealth.

text_flags.why: Likely typo: 'sidhi' is not a word; 'siddhi' (accomplishment) is meant, as in the next unit.
Dual verb form with a singular subject 'bhogaḥ'; the singular 'bhūṣayate' is expected as in the other three occurrences.

notes: The printed tokens are 'sidhirbhūṣayate' and 'bhūṣayete'; the words list uses the corrected forms.

hindi: गुणहीन का रूप हत है, दुःशील का कुल हत है; असिद्ध की विद्या हत है, भोग के अभाव से धन निश्चय ही हत है।
english: Of one without qualities the beauty is destroyed, of one of bad conduct the family is destroyed; of the unaccomplished the learning is destroyed, wealth is indeed destroyed through non-enjoyment.

hindi: भूमि में गया हुआ जल शुद्ध है, पतिव्रता स्त्री शुद्ध है; कल्याण करने वाला राजा शुद्ध है, सन्तोष वाला ब्राह्मण शुद्ध है।
english: Water gone into the ground is pure, a woman devoted to her husband is pure; a king who brings welfare is pure, a brahmin with contentment is pure.
notes: 'santoṣo brāhmaṇaḥ śuciḥ' has no linking word; 'with contentment' is the minimal rendering of the nominative 'santoṣaḥ'. 'bhūmigatam' could also be 'come to the ground'. 'kṣema' is rendered 'welfare' (also 'security').

hindi: असन्तुष्ट द्विज नष्ट हैं और सन्तुष्ट राजा; लज्जायुक्त गणिका नष्ट है और निर्लज्ज कुलाङ्गना।
english: Discontented twice-born are lost, and contented kings; a courtesan with modesty is lost, and a woman of good family without modesty.

text_flags.why: Possible: plural 'nirlajjāḥ' does not agree with the singular 'kulāṅganā'; the singular 'nirlajjā ca' (or plural 'kulāṅganāḥ') is expected.

notes: 'naṣṭāḥ' is carried over to 'santuṣṭāś ca mahībhṛtaḥ' and 'nirlajjā ca kulāṅganā'. The words list uses the corrected 'nirlajjā'. mahībhṛt is literally 'earth-supporter', used as 'king'.

hindi: विद्या से हीन देहधारियों के लिए विशाल कुल से क्या? और विद्वान् का दुष्ट कुल भी, वह देवताओं द्वारा भी पूजा जाता है।
english: Of what use is a large family to embodied beings devoid of learning? And even a bad family of the learned one, even by the gods he is honoured.
notes: The second line does not parse cleanly: 'duṣkulam' (neuter) and 'viduṣaḥ' (genitive) stand beside the nominative 'sa'. It is rendered literally as 'a bad family of the learned one; he is honoured'; the sense is that a learned man of bad family is honoured. No emendation is applied. 'kim kulena' is read as 'what use is the family'.

hindi: विद्वान् संसार में प्रशंसित होता है, विद्वान् सर्वत्र पूजा जाता है; विद्या से सब कुछ पाता है, विद्या सर्वत्र पूजी जाती है।
english: The learned man is praised in the world, the learned man is honoured everywhere; through learning one obtains everything, learning is honoured everywhere.
notes: 'labhate' has no expressed subject ('one').

hindi: ऋण करने वाला पिता शत्रु है, और व्यभिचारिणी माता; रूपवती पत्नी शत्रु है, अपण्डित पुत्र शत्रु है।
english: A father who makes debt is an enemy, and an unchaste mother; a beautiful wife is an enemy, an unlearned son is an enemy.
notes: 'śatruḥ' is carried over to 'mātā ca vyabhicāriṇī'. 'vyabhicāriṇī' is rendered 'unchaste' (literally 'going astray').

hindi: मांस खाने वालों, मदिरा पीने वालों, अक्षर से रहित मुखों वाले, मनुष्य के आकार वाले पशुओं से पृथ्वी बोझ से दबी हुई है।
english: By flesh-eaters, liquor-drinkers and mouths devoid of letters, by beasts of human form, the earth is indeed overcome by burden.
notes: 'māṃsabhakṣyaiḥ' and 'surāpānaiḥ' are taken as adjectives of 'paśubhiḥ', and 'mukhaiḥ akṣaravarjitaiḥ' as a further instrumental phrase ('mouths devoid of letters'). Hindi is idiomatic for the instrumental ('from').

hindi: अन्न से हीन होकर वह राष्ट्र को जला दे, मन्त्र से हीन होकर ऋत्विजों को, दान से हीन होकर यजमान को; यज्ञ के समान शत्रु नहीं है।
english: Devoid of food, it would burn the realm, and devoid of mantras, the priests; devoid of gifts, the sacrificer; there is no enemy equal to sacrifice.
notes: The subject of 'dahet' is not expressed in the unit; the masculine nominatives 'annahīnaḥ' etc. point to 'yajñaḥ' (sacrifice) of the last line, which is supplied as 'it'. mantra is rendered 'mantra' here as the line concerns ritual.
